reason: Dated initial research and causal hypotheses, not a calibrated model

evidence.content: On 16 September 2026 the FOMC raised the policy target to 3.75–4.00%, citing elevated inflation. This is a nominal policy rate, not the real bond yield.

WGC estimated Q2 2026 official-sector net gold purchases near 289 tonnes. The first-half total was 345 tonnes, weaker than other first halves since 2022. Quarterly demand is not a current monthly purchase rate.

EIA attributed volatile and elevated Q2 2026 oil prices partly to disrupted Hormuz flows. A June agreement and more tanker movements coincided with lower oil prices; renewed strikes subsequently increased uncertainty. This is historical transmission evidence.

AP reported an Iranian escalation warning and a tanker strike near Hormuz on 21 September 2026. It reported some transits, but traffic below former levels. This does not establish total closure or its future duration.
Reuters reported spot gold at USD 4,282.98 per troy ounce at 18:05 UTC on 25 September 2026, alongside rising Treasury yields. This is a timestamped spot observation rather than the LBMA fixing.

Working causal hypotheses: shipping disruption can raise energy inflation; tighter policy can lift real yields and the dollar, weighing on gold. Official buying and investor demand may support gold. War can create both safe-haven demand and an opposing rate channel. Edge strengths are judgmental; do not sum shared paths as independent shocks.

edges.description: Hypothesis: further fighting raises transit disruption risk.
Greater effective shipping capacity can ease the energy supply premium.
Persistent energy inflation may induce a tighter policy response.
Tighter policy may raise real yields; inflation expectations and term premium can offset it.
Higher real yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.
Sustained official purchases can support demand at a given supply.
Safe-haven demand may support gold, but its sign must be assessed alongside the rate channel.
